trajectory.content:
# Posting to Slack: resolve the channel, respect exact message wording

Procedure for tasks that require posting a message to Slack.

1. Resolve the channel first: list/search channels and use the exact channel
   name or ID from the task (e.g. `#ops-alerts`), not a guess.
2. If the target is a person (DM), look up their Slack user ID by name/email
   before sending.
3. When the task dictates message content or a template, reproduce it exactly,
   substituting only the dynamic values gathered from earlier steps.
4. For thread replies, pass the parent message's timestamp/thread ID instead of
   posting a new top-level message.
5. Verify the post succeeded from the tool result before reporting done.

# Sending an email with Gmail: find the right tool, required fields, and verify

Procedure for tasks that require sending an email through the Gmail integration.

1. Search for the Gmail send tool (e.g. `gmail_send_email`) before guessing tool names.
2. Resolve the recipient's actual email address first — if the task names a person,
   look them up (contacts, CRM, or a provided sheet) rather than inventing an address.
3. Required fields typically include `to`, `subject`, and `body`. Copy any exact
   wording the task specifies verbatim into the subject/body.
4. If the task asks to CC/BCC or reply in a thread, set those fields explicitly;
   do not send a fresh email when a reply is requested.
5. After sending, confirm the tool result indicates success before reporting done.

# Looking up a row in Google Sheets: locate the spreadsheet, then match exactly

Procedure for tasks that require reading or finding data in a Google Sheet.

1. First list/search available spreadsheets to get the exact spreadsheet and
   worksheet IDs — do not assume names.
2. Read the header row to learn the actual column names before filtering.
3. Use the lookup/search tool with the exact column name and value from the task;
   prefer exact matches, and fall back to scanning rows only for fuzzy criteria.
4. If multiple rows match, re-read the task for a disambiguating field
   (date, status, owner) before picking one.
5. Carry values forward exactly as they appear in the sheet (IDs, emails, amounts) —
   downstream steps are checked against the sheet's literal contents.

- Assume the Slack channel is #deals-acme and post the summary there.
(Please confirm if you want me to make these assumptions; otherwise supply the items above.)

Draft action items extracted (templates — will fill with exact wording/amounts once I review the transcript)
1) Schedule technical deep-dive with Solutions Engineer
   - Owner: Solutions Engineer (SE)
   - Due: within 3 business days
   - Purpose: validate integration requirements and confirm timeline
2) Send proposal & pricing
   - Owner: Account Executive (AE)
   - Due: within 5 business days after technical deep-dive
   - Deliverable: draft proposal with itemized pricing and implementation timeline
3) Collect customer requirements doc / data access checklist
   - Owner: Customer Success / AE
   - Due: 2 business days
   - Notes: request list of systems to integrate, sample data, SSO requirements
4) Legal/Procurement intake (if any procurement/terms discussed)
   - Owner: Legal/Contracts
   - Due: 7 business days or per customer's timeline
   - Deliverable: NDA/contract template or next-step checklist
5) Follow-up call to confirm scope and timeline
   - Owner: AE
   - Due: schedule within 7–10 days
   - Attendees: AE, SE, Customer stakeholders

Follow-up distribution (who I'll notify when you confirm)
- To AE (assign): send follow-up email with action items #2, #5 and attach next steps.
- To SE: send meeting invite and attach discovery notes plus items for technical deep-dive (#1, #3).
- To Legal: send intake info if procurement/terms were raised (#4).
- To Customer Success: add to onboarding pipeline as preliminary stage.

CRM update (template I will apply)
- CRM: [HubSpot or Salesforce — confirm]
- Deal/Opportunity: Acme Corp (ID: [provide])
- New stage: Discovery → Proposed next stage (e.g., "Qualification" or "Proposal")
- Amount: [AMOUNT FROM CALL / TRANSCRIPT — please provide or I will extract from transcript]
- Next step: "Schedule technical deep-dive with SE"
- Close date: [set based on timeline discussed in call; placeholder yyyy-mm-dd if unavailable]
- Description / Notes: short summary of key pain points, stakeholders, and required integrations (I will populate after reviewing transcript)

Slack summary (ready-to-post — I will replace placeholders with exact amounts and details)
Post to: [channel name you provide]

Message draft:
"Discovery Call - Acme Corp (summary)
- Deal: Acme Corp — Amount: [INSERT AMOUNT FROM TRANSCRIPT]
- Key stakeholders: [list names/titles from call]
- Pain points: [bulleted summary]
- Agreed next steps:
  1) Technical deep-dive (owner: SE) — due [date]
  2) Proposal & pricing (owner: AE) — due [date]
  3) Procurement/legal intake (owner: Legal) — due [date]
- Notes: [any constraints, competitive info, timeline urgency]
I'll log the call and add these action items to the CRM. Please react with :+1: if you can own an item or reply to claim ownership."

Example email to assigned SE (I will send once you confirm recipient addresses)
Subject: Technical deep-dive — Acme Corp (requested after discovery)
Body:
"Hi [SE name],
We had a discovery call with Acme Corp. Key items: [short summary]. Can you run a 60-minute technical deep-dive to confirm integration and timeline? Proposed times: [3 options]. Action items to cover: data access, SSO, API limits, timeline, implementation resource needs.
Deal amount discussed: [AMOUNT FROM TRANSCRIPT]
Please confirm availability and I'll schedule.
Thanks, [AE name]"

Next steps for you (pick one)
- Provide the recording link or transcript and the CRM/deal ID + Slack channel; I'll extract exact action items, amounts, update the opportunity, create CRM engagement, and post the summary to the channel.
- Confirm I should proceed using these assumptions (HubSpot, channel #deals-acme) and provide the deal amount to use; I'll then perform the updates and posts.

If you want, I can also:
- Create the HubSpot engagement/note for the call
- Update the HubSpot deal amount & stage
- Post the Slack message and return the results (timestamps/IDs)

Tell me which option you prefer and supply any missing artifacts (recording/transcript and CRM ID / Slack channel). Once I have them I’ll:
- Extract action items and exact amounts from the call
- Assign and send follow-ups to the appropriate owners
- Update the opportunity/deal with the amount/stage/next step
- Post the summary to the deal channel and report back with confirmation + links/IDs of the updates I made.
